plan.title: Treated vs control kidney RNA-seq DE with batch in model
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single bulk RNA-seq experiment: /data/inputs/counts/counts.csv holds raw integer salmon gene-level counts for 12,000 genes x 12 samples (first column is the gene symbol), and /data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv holds 12 rows with condition (6 treated vs 6 control) and batch (two known processing batches, balanced across conditions). The research question is simply which genes differ between treated and control, with batch accounted for.

Because batch is balanced across conditions, batch is not a confounder of the treatment effect but is a nuisance source of variance; the correct handling is to include it as an additive covariate in the differential-expression model (~ batch + condition) rather than to remove it from the counts before testing. Removing batch from counts and then testing would understate residual degrees of freedom and inflate significance. Batch-corrected expression is therefore produced only for visualisation, never for the test.

Step T1S1 builds the analysis-ready object: it joins counts to metadata by sample ID, verifies the 12-sample correspondence and the 6/6 and batch-balance design, filters low-count genes, applies a variance-stabilising/log transform, and produces QC diagnostics — library sizes, sample-sample correlation, PCA coloured by condition and by batch, and the same PCA after batch removal for display only. This quantifies how large the batch effect actually is relative to the treatment effect, which is the single most informative thing to know before reading the DE result.

Step T1S2 runs the differential expression test itself with the design ~ batch + condition, contrast treated vs control, on raw counts; it reports the full result table with shrunken effect sizes where available, BH-adjusted p-values, and an explicit sensitivity comparison against the naive ~ condition model so the reader can see what including batch bought. With n=6 per group the study is modestly powered; the step is required to state the number of genes passing FDR honestly and not to lower thresholds to manufacture hits.

Step T1S3 takes the ranked gene list into functional interpretation. No reference store is currently provisioned, so gene-set resources may be absent at run time; this step is written to resolve whatever pathway/GO resource the environment holds, and to degrade to reporting the ranked list plus descriptive annotation if none is available. The research question survives without it — it is annotation, not the answer.

The package inventory could not be read, so every step must probe its dependencies (DESeq2/edgeR/limma-voom in R, or pydeseq2/statsmodels in Python) and fall back among the equivalent options rather than assume one is installed.
